begin.body: If you have a Bible, use any translation you find easy to read. The references below tell you the book, chapter, and verses. Read slowly. You can also begin with the short introductions here and return to the passages later.

dayOne.title: 1. A welcome home · Luke 15:11–32
dayOne.body: Jesus tells a story about a son who returns home and a father who welcomes him. Read the story and notice how each person responds. What surprises you about the welcome? You can sit with that question without needing an immediate answer.

dayTwo.title: 2. A simple prayer · Matthew 6:9–13
dayTwo.body: Jesus gives his followers a prayer about daily needs, forgiveness, and guidance. Read it one line at a time. If you want to pray, you can begin in your own words with something you’re thankful for or something you need help with.

dayThree.title: 3. Care for a neighbour · Luke 10:25–37
dayThree.body: Jesus tells of someone who stops to care for an injured stranger. Notice who offers practical help. What is one small way you could care for someone today? Return to any of these readings whenever you wish.

common-questions.title: Common questions
common-questions.description: A few starting points for exploring faith, with room to keep asking.

start.title: Where do I start with the Bible?
start.body: The Bible is a collection of books. A Gospel, such as Luke, is one place to begin reading about Jesus. Start with a short passage rather than trying to read everything at once. Our first reading guide offers three places to start.

questions.title: What if I have questions or doubts?
questions.body: You can take time to think and ask questions. Write them down for yourself if that helps. If you choose to talk with someone you trust, you can decide what to share and what to keep private.

pace.title: Do I need to sign up to keep reading?
pace.body: No. These starter guides are free to read without an email address, phone number, or account. You can leave and return whenever you like.

keep-exploring.title: Keep exploring
keep-exploring.description: Simple next steps you can choose for yourself, online or away from a screen.

reread.title: Return to a reading
reread.body: Try reading one of the passages in the first guide again. Notice a word, a question, or an action you missed the first time. There is no progress score or deadline.

talk.title: Choose a conversation
talk.body: If you’d like to talk, consider someone you already trust. You decide whether to have the conversation and what to share. Connection requests and community discovery through Harvest Connect will be available in later releases.

return.title: Keep these guides handy
return.body: Bookmark the starter resources page in your browser to find it again. You can also use the All resources link above to open another guide. No account is needed to return.
